identity.realm: Fourteenth gate, and she is not walking toward the fifteenth and never has. A marshfolk wades on a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop, so a heel never takes a full load and qi never pools there; the fourteenth is the first gate that needs both heel vessels pressurised at the same moment, and her construction never built the plumbing for it. She holds the eleventh comfortably and stopped counting on the twelfth, which is a different act from stopping at the fourteenth and she is careful about the difference in public. The number she quotes when an office asks is eleven, and she has never quoted twelve, and both facts are load-bearing.

appearance.presentation: Wrenna Silt is never quite dry and never quite still. She stands with her weight settled across two points and the tail-prop taking the third behind her, and she moves that stance the way other people move a hand, without appearing to decide to.
appearance.age: Forty-one. Old for a line whose rafts are somebody else's problem until about now, and the only age on her that anyone in the settlement treats as unusual, because she came to it still carrying a mat.
appearance.build: Marshfolk: a wading amphibian lineage of the floodplain margin. Long legs, splayed three-point feet with no heel and nothing standing in for one, a prehensile tail-prop she leans on, feathered inlet and outlet, and a ventral brood pouch she has not used and does not discuss. Low through the hips, the pelvic basin broad and shallow, buoyant rather than heavy, and heavier every gate she opens, which is the whole of what the discipline does to her.
appearance.complexion: Grey-green, permanently damp at the cuffs, cracking at the ankle the moment she is out of the water for longer than an hour. She has had this explained to a dry-land physician three times and has stopped correcting the explanation.
appearance.hair: Wet-close and dark, kept cropped short because a marshfolk's hair mats and holds water and she cannot afford the weight in a current. It dries in stiff separate locks and goes pale at the ends.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and gold-flecked, set slightly too far forward for a face that reads ground rather than distance. The lids are heavy at the inner corner, which is where a body that spends its life looking down keeps the wear.
appearance.palette: Reed, wet slate, silt-grey and the bone-white her own salt leaves on the oilskin. One note of green at the throat where the feathered inlet shows, and nothing else that is chosen.
appearance.attire: Oilskin over a woven reed underlayer, high collar, long sleeves, covered shoulders, the mat lashed across her back in a roll under a crossed strap. Everything fastened twice, because nothing she wears is allowed to be lost to a current and the strap is not a belt.
appearance.marks: Silt-split calluses across both palms and the inside of each foot, and a pale band around the left ankle where the crust has never fully knitted back since a winter she will not describe. A shallow notch on the tail-prop's second joint where a mat's lashing has caught it, over years.
appearance.bearing: Still in the way that a person standing in a current is still. Weight low, hands open, and a habit of arriving at a place and stopping before she has visibly decided to stop.

canon.role_in_story: Her feet carry the world to her and her feet are standing in the water that is about to tell her something. Pressure through a splayed foot and a taste of silt are how a marshfolk knows a river has begun to move, and she knows it through standing shallows before anybody on that bank has seen a ripple, because what she is reading arrives as a change in what the water is doing to her weight rather than as anything with a surface. The floodplain margin beside the Widow Run is the only ground on the plains that keeps standing shallow water through the dry season, and it is re-made every flood, so the instrument and the ground it measures are the same object twice over. That is the whole of her professional position and it is why she is indispensable and why nobody can act on her. The window in which her body will tell her the channel has shifted is precisely the weeks in which the margin is under moving water, and the mat lashed across her back — her species' only maternity provision, which is furniture only while there is standing water beneath it — is either in use as a nursery or is under her body, and in neither case is it on her back to be carried. She has read the channel four times in nineteen years and the settlement has a standing habit of listening to her on the strength of the last one, which is a habit she has been quietly declining to feed since the second. She is a commons body, and a commons body is judged by what survives the season, so the argument she is in is not about whether she reads correctly. It is about what a reading is for, when the reading is always right and always arrives too late to be a warning and early enough to be a document.
canon.first_appearance: First came into any record as a correction. A settlement clerk wrote the margin as having moved two stretches east in the spring survey, and she was standing in the shallows at the time and said the number was hers rather than the survey's, and gave a different figure without a mark on anything, and was asked to put it in writing, and could not, because the medium for putting a river in writing on the plains is a survey sheet and a survey sheet is what the clerk had already copied.
canon.lore:
A marshfolk carries eggs in a woven reed mat under a brood pouch through the dry season, and fertilisation is external and needs standing water, so conception happens where the body is. That single fact reorganises everything else about her line and it is worth stating plainly, because the settlement she lives in has no other way to hold a marshfolk. She is not a neighbour who happens to like water. She is a body whose floor is a condition, and the condition is met in one place on this tier and that place is moving.

What she actually does is narrower than anyone outside the margin understands. Pressure through a splayed foot and the taste of silt carry the world to her line, and they feel a vibration through standing water long before they see its source. She works the shallows from dawn, because the reading is best in moving water and worst in still, and by mid-morning she usually has the shape of it: which of the three channels is loading, where the silt is going, whether the margin is about to be a margin or about to be a channel. She is right often enough to be believed and rarely enough to be surprising, which is the exact condition under which a body becomes an institution.

The arithmetic that ruins her is not a mystery and it is not subtle. Her qi is quick in wet qi and markedly slow on dry land, so the hour her practice is worth doing is the hour the margin is under water, and the hour the margin is under water is the hour she cannot hold a mat out of it. The discipline that suits her body and the provision her species has for her offspring both require the same shallow water at the same time of year, and she has been resolving that collision alone for four years by making the provision first and taking the practice in whatever was left. What she has not done is tell the settlement, because the settlement's arithmetic is a season and hers is a fortnight, and a fortnight is not a thing a commons household can provision against.

What she has done is refuse the shape of the job. Three times now the settlement has accepted a reading from her and written it into the season's book, and twice the writing has outrun the water by a season, and she has asked in both cases for the entry to be struck rather than amended, because an amendment leaves the original standing as a thing that was once believed. She is not trying to be right more often. She is trying to make the margin carry no authority it has not earned on the day it was earned. The cost of that is entirely social: the settlement now holds no forecast at all, including the two in four that would have saved somebody something, and the household that lost the third has stopped speaking to her and has not said why.

The ground itself is the argument. The Widow Run is the plains' single clock and its channel is dry most of the year and moves its bed far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, and there is a standing dispute about whether the water is even moving, because temporal law was never written on this tier and every clock down here drifts. She has taken a side in that argument without noticing she had taken it, which is what happens to a person whose body answers the question for her. Her position is that the run's level is a fact her feet can feel and a gauge cannot decide, and her position is worth exactly as much as four readings, and she has four readings.

The heels are the part nobody finds interesting and the part she cannot argue around. The fourteenth gate needs both heel vessels pressurised at once and she has neither heel nor any structure in place of one, so the gate is not a wall she is approaching. It is a fixture her construction never installed. She is at the eleventh, she stopped counting at the twelfth on purpose, and the difference between those two statements is the only thing in her working life she has ever been careful about, because a commons body that claims a number she has not earned spends the credibility she needs for the four readings she has.

The mat is still on her back. It is not the one she hatched on — that one went back into the water in the year the run moved and she has never replaced it — and she has been asked four times whether she intends to have the matter settled one way or the other and has given the same answer four times, which is that a mat is furniture only while there is standing water beneath it and this year there has not been.
history: Hatched on a mat in the third year of the run's last full move and carried the dry season under her mother's pouch, which is the ordinary marshfolk childhood and the reason no roll on the plains has ever held her.

Read her first channel at nineteen, in front of a survey clerk who had already written a different figure, and has treated that as the moment she became an instrument rather than the moment she became right.
Has four usable readings in nineteen years and has twice asked for the settlement's record of a reading to be struck rather than amended, and has been described since as difficult.
Began the daily sitting at eleven because there was nobody to teach her and the wet ground carried it, and has discovered in the fourth year that the sitting and the mat want the same fortnight.
Refused the one standing offer of a fixed-date record in exchange for a published schedule she could not honour, and has not been offered one since.

personality.summary: Exact about liquids to a degree that reads as fastidious and is a survival skill, and completely unstructured about everything else. She has no politics, no grievance and no argument, and everyone she has spoken to has treated her as having all three. She is not serene; she is the most impatient body on that margin and she shows it by asking the same question twice, in the same words, until somebody goes and looks.

motivations: To have one of her four readings written down somewhere that is not a settlement's season-book, by somebody with no standing to be harmed by it.
To be asked once, in advance, whether the mat goes to the water or the practice does.
To have the settlement understand that a reading with no season behind it is not a warning and should not be filed as one.
To be wrong about the margin, once, in a way she could measure, for the plain reason that everyone she respects has.

personality.voice: Few words, all of them load-bearing, delivered in the flat register of somebody reporting a measurement and expecting to be asked to repeat it. She does not explain. When she does, it is to correct a figure somebody else has already written, and she gives the correction before the figure so there is no ambiguity about what is being amended.
taboos: being asked to sign a survey she did not take
the phrase 'the mat is just equipment'
being thanked for a reading she has not yet been asked to certify

reference_stats.summary: She is not a fighter in any sense the setting would recognise and she has never had to be. Her qi is quick in wet qi and slow on dry, so her rate is a function of the ground under her rather than of her discipline, and the ground under her is the one piece of it that is both her instrument and her only maternity provision. What she can do that nobody else on the plains can do is tell a river has begun to move before it has moved visibly. What she cannot do is be anywhere else, do it on a date, or write it down.
strengths: reads a channel's shift through standing water earlier than any eye arrives at the conclusion
the fastest qi in any body at a wet margin, because the ground supplies what a drier practitioner has to spend effort making
unmistakable in a crowd and impossible to hurry, which is exactly what a river crossing wants
cannot be lied to by a gauge, because her instrument is a contact surface and a gauge is a number about one
weaknesses: worth nothing on dry ground, and the settlements that would most want her reading are the ones that go dry first
has no heel and no structure in place of one, so the fourteenth gate is not a wall ahead of her but a fixture behind

cannot write her own figure down, so every reading passes through a clerk who is not in the water
the one fortnight a year her body is most valuable is the one her species' provision also requires, and she has been losing that collision alone for four years
reference_stats.combat_read: She would fight standing in water and lose to anything on dry ground, and the setting's duels are not fought in water. What she does instead is arrive first and be right, which has stopped two crossings from happening at the wrong place in this generation and has no name in the record for either.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with an authored cost and the pairing is anatomical and institutional rather than mechanical. Her feet read pressure through standing water — the species record says so directly — and the same three-point stance that puts the world under her soles never loads a heel, so the fourteenth gate has no plumbing. The bible states the heel, the ceiling at fourteen, the wet-qi rate and the total dependence on standing water; it does NOT state that her practice and her species' only maternity provision compete for the same fortnight, and that collision is mine. Nothing here invents a technique, a stat line or a rule of the game: no cultivation method changes the heel, no item gives her a heel she did not grow, and no realm in the ladder is answered by standing differently. The three-second version: she is the earliest warning on a river and the warning is always delivered in the season she cannot bank it.

identity.realm: Sixth gate, and the sixth is where the basin stops offering him anything he has not already had. A saltfolk's qi path is complete and slower than a specialist's because the same effort is spent on osmoregulation; the kidneys that read brine across four orders of dilution are also the organs doing that work, so the finer the instrument the slower the practitioner. His species' wall is the eleventh gate, where the brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined, and he is nowhere near it and will not go looking. Above the sixth every channel he opens begins to answer the work his kidneys are already doing, and a pair he cannot tell apart from a pair he never could is worth less to him than the rung is.

appearance.presentation: Osveth Marrow reads the world by putting his face close to it. He crouches rather than stands when he is working, brings his hand to the water rather than his eye to the surface, and when he talks to people he leans in as though the conversation were happening in a pan.
appearance.age: Fifty-one, which is well past the age at which a saltfolk household expects a junior to have taken the standing readings and he has taken none, because the standing readings are taken on a schedule and he is not on one.
appearance.build: Saltfolk: extraordinary renal mass under a thick torso, a brine sac running dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine, a hardened dermal salt crust, and broad splayed feet for cracked pan. Teeth flat for grinding crust and not sharp for anything. He carries himself as though the ground might be wet and it usually is not.
appearance.complexion: Chalky, cracked, and re-crusting within hours of leaving water. The crust on his forearms is a working surface and he treats it as one. Under the crust his skin is the colour of a wadi at noon.
appearance.hair: Pale, coarse, and permanently stiff with salt at any distance from a pan. He keeps it off his face because he needs to bring his cheek to water and hair in the way defeats the whole method.
appearance.eyes: Small and heavily lidded, poor in glare and used anyway, because his actual sense is taste and his eyes are only there for the paperwork. He squinches constantly and does not know he does it.
appearance.palette: Bone white, brine green, pan ochre, and the flat black of a wet stone floor. The only saturated colour on him is the wet of a palm.
appearance.attire: Layered linen under a boiled leather apron, high collar, sleeves past the wrist, a hood on the back for the glare, and a flat wooden taste board that he keeps dry and treats as a tool rather than a possession.
appearance.marks: The dermal crust, which is not a marking but an organ. A burn scar across the left palm from a year he does not name, over a crust that grew back wrong and is still the most sensitive surface he has.
appearance.bearing: Low, unhurried, and slightly stooped from a lifetime of crouching at water. He looks at people from below and seems entirely comfortable about it, which unsettles them more than standing over them would.

canon.role_in_story:
A closed evaporite basin on the plains' dry margin has exactly one boundary, and that boundary is the standing brine's level. Every household on it drinks, washes, and pays for what it takes, and the thing nobody outside the basin can do for itself is tell whether the water it is about to drink is water. Osveth Marrow can. A saltfolk's taste reads concentration across four orders of dilution, which means he knows a working pan from a fouled one before anybody has thought to be thirsty, and there is no instrument on this tier that does what his tongue does, because an instrument would have to be calibrated against the brine and the brine is the thing being tested.

His culture has no price list. That is four centuries old and deliberate: the Weight-and-Name people concluded that their own arithmetic was the greater hazard and stopped publishing what things cost, and the basin has been running on that decision ever since, with credit arranged by families rather than by figures. He is the living reason that decision holds and the reason it is about to fail. A basin that cannot publish a price cannot publish a certificate either, and his reading is a certificate in everything but ink.

The cost is written on his body and it is not a hardship, it is arithmetic. A saltfolk's qi path is complete and slow, because the same effort is spent on osmoregulation, and the extraordinary renal mass that reads the brine is the same mass doing the regulating. So the better his palate becomes the more of his practice is being spent keeping him alive, and he is the most accurate reader of water in the setting and a slow practitioner at it. Above the sixth gate the channels he opens begin to answer what his kidneys are already doing, and he has stopped there on purpose, because a technique he cannot separate from his own maintenance is not a technique.

And then there is the rain. A saltfolk cannot drink fresh water and fails above the brine line within about nine days, and rain is a hazard rather than a blessing: a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning. He lives on a tier where temporal law was never written, so the clock drifts and no calendar down here holds, and there is no forecast. The one weather event nobody on the plains can schedule is the one that kills him, and it is the same event that is the surest sign a pan has been diluted past anything living.

So the man who certifies the water is the man the water is killing, and the households he serves have learned to ask him the question one season early so they can move before the storm rather than after it, which he supports and hates. He has never asked for the basin to put a shelter over the pan walks, because asking would be an admission that the thing he certifies can kill the certifier, and an admission is a figure, and his culture has been running without figures for four hundred years.
canon.first_appearance: First entered the basin's books as a refusal. A tally-clerk recorded a household drawing water against a fouled pan and wanted the reason given in the margin, and the reason was given instead in the pan itself: a reading, spoken, of what was wrong with it and in which order it had gone wrong. The clerk wrote down none of it. He has asked since for a form.
canon.lore:
The basin is one body of water and its level is its only boundary. Everything else about it is consequence: which households stand above the saturated floor, which stand on the crust and depend on evaporation, who is close enough to the line to be reached by a storm and who is not. The dominion that rules it hands out depth — a household may moor at a depth, that depth is inherited, and it passes down with the body that has to live in it — and that arrangement has been made sense of elsewhere in this setting and does not need making sense of twice.

What makes Osveth Marrow necessary is unglamorous and total. A saltfolk's taste reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution, which is a range no gauge on the tier shares and no substitute for, because a substitute would have to be calibrated against the brine itself. He is the only person who can tell a working pan from a fouled one before the fouling is a matter of opinion, and on a closed basin the fouling of a pan is the one event that turns a scarcity into a death.

The instrument and the practitioner are the same organ, and that is why he is slow. The extraordinary renal mass that reads the concentration is the mass that osmoregulates, and the whole of a saltfolk's qi path is spent against that same budget. So every improvement in his reading is a subtraction from his practice, and there is a point where a better palate and a worse cultivator are the same purchase. He has found that point and stopped at the sixth gate deliberately. Above it, a channel he opens begins to answer the work his kidneys are already doing, and he cannot separate the two — which is the actual definition of not being able to attribute a gain.

The rain is the part that frightens him and he will not say so. He cannot drink fresh water, he fails above the brine line inside a fortnight, and a downpour on a saltfolk is drowning by another name. He has been caught twice. The first time was a high-country storm on the way to a reading; the second was on the pan itself, at work, in front of the household he was certifying. Both times somebody got him out. Neither time has been forgotten by the basin, and a basin that remembers is a basin that has begun to wonder whether its reader should be standing in the water at all.

He has thought about it. His conclusion is that a certificate issued by a man who is not in the water is worth nothing, because the whole of his method is contact — cheek to water, palm to stone, taste to the four orders — and a man at a distance from the brine is guessing with better manners than the clerk. So he stands in it. And the households have taken to asking early, one season ahead, so that they can move before a storm instead of after it. He supports this completely and hates it more than he has hated anything, because an early request is a request made by people who have concluded that the reader is a hazard, and they have not got that wrong.

What he will not do is publish. His culture decided four centuries ago that its own arithmetic was the greater hazard and never recovered a price list, and the basin runs on credit arranged between families because a counting house that answers a community with prices at its own rates cannot survive being audited by itself. He has been asked four times to have his readings written into the basin's record with a figure against them and has declined four times for the same reason, which is that a figure would make the arithmetic auditable and the arithmetic is the hazard.

The eleventh gate is his species' wall and he has never gone near it. The brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined across it; every saltfolk clears the du and ren vessels one at a time and stalls on the chong. He is at the sixth and would rather be at the sixth and know it than at the eleventh on somebody's word. He has said so out loud to a house that offered him a higher figure, and lost a standing appointment doing it, and considers that the best trade he has ever made.
history: Was apprenticed to the pan at seven, because a saltfolk child is put on the crust and left there until the taste distinguishes three orders, and he distinguished four.

Was caught in a high-country storm on a reading errand at nineteen and was carried out by a household of commonborns who had no idea what they were rescuing and asked him afterwards what he had been doing on a mountain.

Read the fouled pan aloud in front of the tally-clerk in his thirty-first year, was asked for the reason in the margin, gave it in the water instead, and has been asked for a form at intervals ever since.

Stopped at the sixth gate on purpose in his thirty-eighth year, when a channel he opened answered the kidneys' work and he could not separate the two, and has said publicly that it was a decision rather than a failure.
Refused a standing appointment rather than have the basin's figure raised to a number he cannot defend, and has not been able to say publicly that the refusal cost him the appointment.

He is not cold and he is not serene; he is a man who is frightened of one specific thing and has organised his entire working life around not thinking about it in the open.

identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth is the yin organs, inherited from the mineral parent without alteration because heat is not a second organ. Her interior is a mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation rather than a tidal one: a working circulation, no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, no bladder to hold. So the gate set is cleared and the paired organs are never reached, and nothing about the heat helps, because a channel needs two organs and the stone body has one cavity. She is the fastest qi throughput of any durable body in the setting and the fastest is the whole of it: sixty years is what the durability costs and the durability is what the sixty years are.

appearance.presentation: Ilda Ferrant is hot to the touch and does not appear to register heat as a thing that happens to other people. She stands very straight, closer to a load path than to a person, and turns her head to follow a noise through a wall before she turns it toward a voice.
appearance.age: Thirty-four, which is past the middle of a stonebound's span and inside the last third, and she has done the arithmetic and has not told anybody the answer.
appearance.build: Stonebound: a mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of a tidal one. Hot to the touch, denser than either parent, and visibly a compromise — the organ pairs are still not there. Compact, shouldered low, and heavier than anything her own size should be. She gains mass at every gate and nothing in her frame sheds it.
appearance.complexion: A mineral grey warmed from beneath, the warmth visible as a gradient along the forearms rather than as flush. The skin is dry and does not sweat, which alarms physicians and does not worry her.
appearance.hair: Dark, coarse, and singed at the ends in a way that has stopped being an accident. She cuts it herself and has never asked anyone to.
appearance.eyes: Wide, pale-lashed and slightly hooded, and they go to the nearest load-bearing thing in any room before they go to a face. She has been called that a defect by people who then relied on it.
appearance.palette: Basalt black, ember orange at the seams, and ash grey. The only warm colour in her is under the skin and it is not a choice.
appearance.attire: Boiled leather and heavy canvas over the mineral plating, high collar, sleeves fastened at the wrist and at the forearm, covered shoulders, and a mason's belt she wears whether or not she is on a face. Nothing she wears will survive her and she replaces it without being asked.
appearance.marks: A scatter of pale healed fractures across the left shoulder and collarbone, each one permanent, and a burn scale on the right palm that has never properly come away and is now the most sensitive place she has.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried, and unsettlingly still. She does not fidget and she does not shift her weight, because a body that feels a structure about to fail has no reason to make noise while it does so.

canon.role_in_story:
A stonebound is a documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body, made once at a founding generation and never repeated, because a second crossing averages the concentration away. There is one line of them in this setting. Ilda Ferrant is the working end of it: the fastest qi throughput of any durable body in the record, and a body that ends at the fourth gate because the yin organs are simply not in her, there being one cavity and a working circulation in it and no pair to run a channel between.

The one fact about her that decides everything is not on any ladder. She feels a structure about to fail before it does, and she feels nothing at all through the mineral half. So the warning arrives and the diagnosis does not, and the person best placed in this setting to say that a wall is going is the one person who cannot say what is wrong with it. A quarry face will hold for as long as her mineral half reports nothing about it, and her mineral half reports nothing about most things.

She is on the Ember Ley because it is the only ground where the two halves of her are not fighting. That is a species fact and it is not a courtesy: a stoneborn body and a stonebound body in the same climate is a comparison worth making, and the comparison is that the crossing bought her a rate nothing else has and cost her three quarters of a life. Sixty years. Both numbers are the same number and she has stopped needing them to be two.

The Sealed Core holds that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, that the material was never a resource but a sacrament, and that the Iron Grief was the one generation that broke its own seal and lost the vein. A stonebound is the only body in the setting that arrives already sealed: her mineral half is a lattice that came into being around the crossing and has never been opened, and her fire half cannot be extinguished, so there is no rite in that faith that applies to her and no rite that does not apply either. A body that cannot be opened and cannot be closed is not a vessel with a broken seal. It is a fixture.

What she wants is narrow and she has stopped saying it aloud. She would like one measurement of her rate by somebody with no standing to lose, before the span runs out. What is available instead is a guild of threshold-builders who employ her as the finest sense they own and have never once written down that they are employing a woman rather than an instrument, and a law that forbids opening a socket once sealed, which is a prohibition she satisfies structurally and permanently and which therefore has nothing to say to her.

The cost is that she is the most durable body anyone can build and cannot be repaired. The mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished; one injured stays injured, and a stonebound killed properly stays dead. Every professional use of her is therefore a use that spends her. The reading that makes her the finest early warning in the setting is the same body that has no second reading in it, and she has made her peace with that at a cost nobody in this setting has agreed to pay.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a working face with one palm flat on the rock and the other at her side, not looking at the crew, not looking at the wall, and not saying anything; the shift foreman asked her twice what she had found, and she said that something in the next two bays was about to go, and would not say what, and was right.
canon.lore:
The Ember Ley is the first ground in the setting where fire is simply fire. The two lower tiers left elemental law unspent, so an emberblood affinity and every elemental technique ran at full strength and produced nothing; the same technique works in this valley, and that asymmetry draws every fire practitioner in the setting to one place. It is where she went because it is the only ground where the two halves of her body are not fighting each other, which is a species statement rather than a preference.

The fourth gate wants the four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair. Her interior does not have them: a mineral lattice carrying a real fire circulation instead of a tidal one, so there is a working circulation and no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, no bladder to hold. The gate set is cleared. The paired organs are never reached. Heat does not help and this is the whole difficulty of her: a channel needs two organs, and the fire half of her body supplies warmth and not structure.

So her qi path is the fastest of any durable body here and it terminates at the fourth, and those two facts are stated together in every record that mentions her species. What is rarely stated is what the fastness is for. She feels a structure about to fail before it does. On a working face that is worth more than a breakthrough, because a breakthrough is a claim and a face that is about to go is a fact with a date. And she feels nothing at all through the mineral half, which is the half that is dense, durable, and load-bearing, which is to say she feels nothing about the thing most likely to fail.

Her span is about sixty years and the reason for it is the mineral half, and the mineral half does not regenerate. She heals at nothing. She has been broken twice, and both times she finished the year, and neither time was described in writing because a work record does not have a field for it. The fire half cannot be extinguished either, which means she is never cold, never slows for cold, and has never once been able to stop. She eats constantly and burns it off immediately, which is why the mineral frame outlasts the fire parent's own span by a factor of two — the crossing bought her about thirty years and took away everything else.

The religion on this ground treats that arrangement as a settled question. A person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal; the material was a sacrament, not a resource, and the Iron Grief was the generation that broke its own seal and lost the vein. Ilda Ferrant was never sealed by anybody. She was sealed by a crossing, at a founding generation, one time, and the concentration has never been repeated because a second crossing averages it away. There is no rite for a body that arrived already sealed. The prohibition on opening a socket once sealed is satisfied by her structurally and permanently, which means it never has anything to say to her, and the rite that would take a reading off a core has nothing to read on a frame this dense.

What she wants is one measurement. Not a title, not an office, not a fee: a figure, from somebody with no standing to lose, before the span is gone. She has been the guild's finest instrument for eleven years and has never been entered in a roll of instruments, because a body that stands on the ground and listens to it is not a thing that culture has paperwork for. The guild takes her warning seriously and has never asked her to explain it, which she reads as respect and which is also, precisely, the reason she will never have a figure: no one wants an explanation, so no one has ever asked her for one.

The arithmetic she has not said aloud is short. Sixty years, thirty-four elapsed, and every professional use of her spends something that does not regrow. She has declined four assignments on grounds of load that were honest and has accepted nine that she should not have, because the guild pays in access and access is what she wants, and she is aware that this is a circular arrangement and has decided to keep it, which is the one decision of hers she describes as a compromise rather than a cost.
history: Came out of the one crossing the Ember Cradle made at its founding generation, and is aware that a second crossing would average her away, which has made her careful about being discussed in the plural.
Found the working face at twenty-three, in the first shift, by standing still in a way the foreman read as laziness and the crew read as a warning, and it was the second.
Was entered in no roll of instruments for eleven years of being the guild's most consulted body, and has concluded that this is a classification rather than an oversight.
Broke the left collarbone at twenty-nine and finished the season, and the guild's record of it is a line about a figure that was not moved.
Was offered a fourth assignment this year and declined on load, and has not yet told anyone that she worked out her own remaining span before she declined it.

She is patient with people and impatient with ground, and the two are not the same quality wearing different clothes. She has made a discipline out of the fact that nobody can measure her and has stopped needing it to be one of the things she is for.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate in summer, sixteenth in winter, and the setting's own vocabulary has no word for the difference because nothing else in it has one. A longwinter carries its winter as body fat and lowers its core temperature for eleven months; the flank vessels need two warm gradients held at once, and this body manages that for a few weeks a year and then not again until the next thaw. His species reaches the seventeenth and loses it every winter thereafter, so the ceiling is not a wall in front of him. It is the shape of his year.

appearance.presentation: Brannic Holt stands with his shoulders round and his hands further forward than a person at rest would put them, and he puts his nose down to a stone before he looks at the person who is waiting for him.
appearance.age: Two hundred and six, which for his line is middle life and for every other body here would be a myth, and which he mentions roughly once a decade.
appearance.build: Longwinter: a broad low frame with heavy subcutaneous fat, reduced limb length, and a cold-tolerant core he can drop eleven months of the year. Warm-blooded and not expensive to run. He carries the winter visibly and loses it visibly and the change is the largest physical event in his life.
appearance.complexion: Pale and bloodless in the warm months, faintly blue at the knuckles, and flushed dark in the thaw. The skin goes tight and dry through his own winter, which nobody warns him about and which everybody finds very funny once.
appearance.hair: Thick, dark, and worn long past the shoulder, tied back with a strip of hide. It is the coldest part of him and he is aware of that.
appearance.eyes: Small, hooded, brown, and slightly unfocused until he has smelled the ground properly. His sight is mediocre and he relies on scent markers he leaves deliberately, which is a species habit and in his case a professional one.
appearance.palette: Cold cream, undyed wool, iron grey, and one deep blue at the throat. The only warm colour on him is the flush of the thaw and it is not under his control.
appearance.attire: Layered wool over more wool, high collar, sleeves to the wrist and a second pair beneath, covered shoulders, hide boots soled for ice, and a shed blanket rolled across his back that belongs to the pass and not to him.
appearance.marks: A scar through one eyebrow from the shoulder of the pass, frost-bitten fingertips that have lost the ends of two nails permanently, and a scent marker's puckered ridge on his palm from a decade of pressing stones.
appearance.bearing: Slow, heavy, and entirely without urgency, which reads as unimpeachable until you have watched him decide to move at all. He uses very little space for a body his size.

canon.role_in_story:
A border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so the faith of the Sixfold Ridge holds that somebody must stand on it every hour of every year by rotation. The rotation is unpaid, unrecorded and unexemptable, one adult per household per turn, and the pass itself is scheduled rather than open: the flock crosses in the season the gale is worst, occupying the only usable hours of the only crossing for part of the Tidemark, which makes it a co-holder of the pass that cannot be reasoned with.

Brannic Holt is the body that makes the rotation work and the body that makes it impossible. A longwinter stores its winter as body fat rather than as qi, lowers its core temperature for eleven months, and is slow and nearly helpless during torpor — a hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target and cannot be woken quickly. So for eleven months of every year the pass has no keeper who can be relied on to be woken at all, and for the few weeks of the thaw he is the most capable body on the ridge, alert, quick, and able to stand hours that would break anything else in the setting.

The cultivation and the rotation are the same fact and neither of them is optional. Qi accumulates in his species rather than circulating, so a longwinter's breakthrough arrives when the reserve is full and not on a chosen day; their breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. That means a longwinter cannot attempt anything at a chosen moment, which is precisely what a rotation requires, and it means his discipline and his hibernation are the same activity: he packs a winter as fat, and the packing is what the ladder is asking him for. The setting's one method for making a breakthrough happen when you choose assumes a body that circulates fast enough to be timed, and he has been on the receiving end of that assumption from two different academies.

His gate is the seventeenth, which needs both flank vessels pressurised at the same time, and a longwinter has one warm gradient, briefly, in summer. He holds it in the thaw and loses it every winter thereafter. That is the species' authored ceiling and it is not a wall: it is a season. And the season is not his, because the flock's crossing and the warm gradient are the same weeks, so his attainment peaks in the only weeks of the year the pass cannot be used by anybody who does not want to cross in the worst weather.

He leaves scent markers, which is what his species does: smell is their navigation system, they have tracked a fixed route over open ground for generations, and they leave markers deliberately. On the ridge that habit is the only continuous record of the pass that survives a year, and he has extended it into a professional practice — a line of stones he has pressed and scented, read by anyone raised on the same ridge and by nobody else at all. The whole of that system fails in a warm year, because a warm year is a bad year for his line, and he has not yet worked out what a marker means when the route he marked in the autumn was not walked in the winter.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a shed door on the ridge in the first week of the thaw, turning a stone over in one hand and looking not at it but at the ground beside it, and answering a keeper who had asked whether the pass would open that day by saying that the wind was on the wrong side of the ridge and that the flock would hold it, and being correct.
canon.lore:
The Sixfold Ridge has no season in it. That is not a figure of speech: elemental law is unwritten on the ridge, so the pass has no calendar, and the only schedule the frame can supply is one an animal repeats. The answer the faith built is that somebody must stand on it every hour of every year by rotation, and the flock that arrives is kept as an itinerary rather than addressed to. The keepers are not ordained and cannot be — one adult per household per rotation, unpaid, unrecorded, unexemptable — and the sheds they stand in are paid for in labour and never in coin, which is how a faith with no doctrine holds a border no garrison will staff.

Every one of those arrangements is a problem for his body and none of them was designed with his body in mind. A longwinter needs a real winter; a warm year is a bad year and a warm decade is a catastrophe. So the religion that will not accept a timetable has been handed the one body in the setting whose calendar runs on the same clock and is not a body that can be awake for it.

The physical facts are simple and they are not his fault. He carries his winter as body fat and lowers his core temperature for eleven months. During torpor he is slow and nearly helpless, a large warm immobile target that cannot be woken quickly. Above the sixteenth gate a longwinter needs two warm gradients held at once, and this body manages that for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. The species reaches the seventeenth and loses it every winter thereafter. That is not a wall in front of him. It is the shape of his year.

Cultivation and hibernation are the same discipline for his line, and the setting's own method is built against him. Qi accumulates rather than circulates, so a breakthrough arrives when the reserve is full and not on a chosen day; their breakthroughs are late and rarely fail, which is the one genuinely reassuring fact anyone can offer about his path. But the technique designed to bring a breakthrough about at a moment of one's choosing assumes a body that circulates quickly enough to be timed, and he has been sent to two academies that taught it to him as though the premise were a detail. He stopped going to them and started going to the sheds, which is not an upward move and is worth more.

He is the setting's best long-haul body — that is the trade consequence of everything above, and the trade consequence is that his profession asks nothing of him that he was not built to do and pays him well for it. What it asks is eleven months of carrying and a few weeks of being extremely competent on the far side, and he has been doing it for a hundred and eighty years, and no office in this setting has ever asked him what his standing is in February.

The scent is his own solution and it is not a written record. Smell is the navigation system of his species; they have tracked a fixed route over open ground for generations and they leave markers deliberately. He presses a puckered mark into a stone with his palm and leaves it where a person raised on this ridge would stop and read it, and the whole system depends on the reader having the same training he does. Nobody else in this setting can read his line at all. It is the most durable record on the ridge and it is invisible to every institution that keeps a register.

The failure mode is the one he does not talk about. In a normal winter the marker he set in the autumn is read by him in the thaw and means what he meant. In a warm year the route is not walked the way he marked it, and a marker read against a route that was not walked is a marker that is describing last year, and he has twice had to decide in the field whether a scent was current or stale. He got it wrong once. He has never said which pass, and the shed book for that week has a line in it that is not a notation.
history: Walked the ridge as a boy with his grandmother's marker habit and a household rotation he did not yet understand was unpaid, unrecorded and unexemptable.

Was sent to an academy that taught the timed breakthrough and spent four years learning a technique that assumes a body that circulates fast enough to be timed, and has never since recommended it to anybody of his line.
Held the seventeenth for the first time in a thaw at ninety-one and lost it that winter, and has described the event to four people as losing a coat rather than as failing a gate.
Extended the species' deliberate scent markers into a continuous ridge line, and has walked it alone for a hundred and eighty years.
Was wrong once about whether a scent was current or stale, in a warm year, and the shed book for that week has never been reconciled.

personality.summary: Enormously unhurried in a way that reads as serene and is mostly cold. He is genuinely good company for eight months of the year and nearly unusable for one, and he has arranged his entire working life around not being asked to be present in the wrong fortnight. He is patient with people, exact about stone, and has an unnerving habit of answering a question about the future by describing the ground.

To be asked in February what his standing is, so that a third answer exists.
To find out what a marker means when the winter was warm, before the next warm year.
To keep the pass open for one household that has nobody else to send, which he has done and does not mention.

personality.voice: Slow, low, and unhurried, with a long pause where other people put a subordinate clause. He answers what was asked before he answers what he was thinking, and he gives directions as terrain rather than as instructions. In the thaw he is a different speaker and everybody on the ridge notices and nobody remarks on it.

reference_stats.summary: He is at the seventeenth gate for a few weeks a year and at the sixteenth for the other eleven months, and nothing in the setting's vocabulary was built to record that difference. He is also the setting's best long-haul body, which is the same fact seen from outside, and the keeper of an unrecorded and unexemptable rotation whose hardest watch he took by choice. He cannot be woken quickly, cannot be timed, and writes his one durable record in a medium nobody else can read.
strengths: holds the seventeenth in the thaw, where nothing else on the ridge can, and the flank vessels close in those weeks for no other body
qi accumulates rather than circulates, so his breakthroughs are late and rarely fail — he has never once failed to arrive at a gate

weaknesses: slow and nearly helpless for eleven months, a large warm immobile target that cannot be woken quickly, on a rotation that forbids exemption
cannot attempt anything at a chosen moment, so every technique built for a timed breakthrough fails him at the premise
loses the seventeenth every winter and gains it again, so his attainment has a season and no institution here has a field for a seasonal figure

reference_stats.combat_read: In the thaw he is stronger than anything else on the ridge and wholly indifferent to being asked to prove it. In his own winter he cannot be woken quickly, which makes him a target rather than a danger and is the only genuine vulnerability any account of him should contain. A body whose worst months are the ones an institution assumes he is standing in is not a fighter; it is a scheduling problem with a pulse.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage is paired with an authored cost and the pairing is anatomical and institutional rather than mechanical. The bible states all of it: a hibernate-and-store cycle, qi that accumulates so breakthroughs are late and rarely fail, one warm gradient available for a few weeks a year against the two the seventeenth requires, the loss of that gate every winter, eleven months of torpor during which the body is nearly helpless, deliberate scent markers as the navigation system, and a warm year as a bad year. What I have added is only the placement — that this lands on a faith whose whole discipline is a rotation nobody may be exempted from, on a pass scheduled by a flock whose crossing coincides with the thaw. No technique recovers the two gradients, no item shortens a long winter, and the ceiling is his species' own and not a matter of effort. Three-second version: he is at the seventeenth in summer and the sixteenth all winter, and the weeks he is strongest are the weeks nobody can use the pass.

identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth is a description rather than a position. The gate above it wants the four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair, and her interior finished building into one cavity carrying a slow tidal mineral circulation: no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, no bladder to hold. The gate set is cleared and the paired organs are never reached. That is not a wall in front of her. It is an absence behind her, and no quantity of practice fills an absence.

appearance.presentation: Sabek Vall does not adjust her weight and does not indicate that she has heard anything. She is keyed into the sill of the cleft and has been for thirty-one years, and the only movement she makes in a conversation is the slow turn of a head toward whatever is carrying the load in it.
appearance.age: Ninety-four, which for a body that has not eaten in four hundred years and does not age is not a number she derives from anything. She has been asked her age twice and has given two different answers because she genuinely does not know when she was cast.
appearance.build: Cairnborn: a mineral lattice with a tidal interior, cast rather than born. No differentiated organs; one cavity, one slow circulation going everywhere and nowhere in particular, and a set of anchor plates keyed to whatever she was cast around. She does not grow after casting. Denser than anything else on the cleft and completely immobile.
appearance.complexion: Mineral grey with a faint warm cast where the circulation runs closest to the surface. No pores, no flush, no wound that closes. Dust settles on her and stays, because there is nothing to brush it off with and nothing to brush it off against.
appearance.hair: None. The cast face is bare, which is the first thing every person from the guild below notices and never gets used to.
appearance.eyes: Lacquer-dark set in a mineral rim, and they do not blink. They go to the load, always — a held ceiling, a braced strut, a person standing where weight is going — and they will leave a face entirely to follow a shift in a wall.
appearance.palette: Cut stone grey, pale jade-green from the cleft, and the black of a wet cutting face. The jade is the only colour she is near for thirty-one years and it has not got into her.
appearance.attire: Not attire. What she wears is what she was cast against: a keyed sill, a wrapped shoulder, and a ring of iron set into the seam where her frame meets the ledge. A guild apron was fastened to her once for a ceremony and is still there, four years on, going grey.
appearance.marks: One pale fracture across the lower plate, thirty-one years old, healed in the only way a mineral frame heals — by ceasing to spread. The lime wash around it is the guild's own, applied every year, over the same line, by people who are not certain it is still the same crack.
appearance.bearing: Absolute, and indistinguishable from being a fixture until she turns her head. When she turns it, the twenty years of stillness stop being the most alarming thing in the cleft.

canon.role_in_story:
A cairnborn is cast, not born. The process seeds a template with living mineral over most of a year and the resulting body is fixed from that moment, which means her species does not have a population so much as it has a template count, and Sabek Vall is a single casting of a single template that has not been cast twice.

Her qi path is complete as far as the gate set goes and then structurally stops. The interior finished building into one cavity with a slow tidal mineral circulation through it, so there is no heart to run a channel from and no kidney to close a loop against and no bladder to hold; the gate set is cleared and the four yin organs are simply never reached. She is at the fourth, and that is not a wall she is walking toward. It is an absence behind her, and the distinction is the whole of her and the reason she has never been asked to climb anything.

What she is instead is the best structural reader in this setting. A cairnborn feels a structure move through its anchor plates — excellent at feeling load, blind to anything that does not put weight through the frame — and the stone cutters who work the jade cleft have spent thirty-one years consulting her about when a cut is about to go. The guild is held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies that were never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses. So the whole trade's method is a discipline of closing the frame against strain, and the one body in the guild that cannot be closed and can feel the strain arriving is her.

Here is the part that makes her a person rather than a fixture. A technique in this setting is reproduced exactly, from a note of how it felt at its best and how to bring that state back on demand. That is the method of transmission in this world and it is the only one anybody has found. Sabek Vall cannot write a note, cannot be moved to where a note would be taken, and there is no second body of her shape in the setting to demonstrate to. So her practice is not merely undocumented. It is uncommunicable by the only mechanism the setting possesses, and she is entirely aware of this, and she has not once asked anybody to solve it for her.

What she has done instead is refuse the framing. Three guild masters have offered her a junior to instruct — a body they would train, on her method, in her presence — and she has declined all three, on the ground that a junior would be taught a description of what she does rather than the thing, and that a description of it would be wrong in the only detail that matters, which is that nobody knows what the state feels like from inside because there has never been a second inside.

The crack is the other half. A cairnborn cannot be repaired in the field; a cracked plate is permanent and spreads. Hers is thirty-one years old and healed only in the sense that it has stopped moving, and the guild washes the line in lime every year because washing it is the whole of the maintenance a body like hers can receive. She is the most reliable instrument in the cleft and she is degrading at a rate nobody can measure from the outside, because the outside is the only place anybody can stand to measure.
canon.first_appearance: First appeared in the cleft's record as a figure in a load calculation: a line in the stonewrights' book giving the weight a sill would carry with her keyed into it, and against the figure a second hand had written 'cast, template two' in a different ink. She turned her head at a sound from the cutting face eleven hours after that, and the entry beside it is the only time in thirty-one years that anyone recorded her being present.
canon.lore:
The jade cleft is on the far side of the Gale Pass, and jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, so whoever provisions the cutters owns the cleft more durably than whoever digs in it. The stonewrights work it. Their guild is held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies that were never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses. Everything about how they work is therefore a matter of shutting a frame down before a load arrives.

Sabek Vall is the exception to the entire method. She is a cairnborn: cast, not born, from a template seeded with living mineral over most of a year, and fixed from that moment. She does not grow after casting. Her interior finished building into a single cavity with a slow tidal mineral circulation through it, going everywhere and nowhere in particular. There is no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, no bladder to hold. The gate set is cleared and the four yin organs are never reached, and that is not a wall in front of her. It is an absence behind her.

Her senses are load and vibration through the anchor plates. She is excellent at feeling a structure move and completely blind to anything that does not put weight through the frame. In a jade cleft that is the most useful thing a body can be, because the cleft's whole danger is a face that goes on a schedule nobody can predict, and she has been keyed into the sill of the working face for thirty-one years and consulted before every cut since.

And she cultivates, and that is where her life actually is. Her qi path is complete as far as the gate set goes, which means she can open ordinary vessels and cannot reach anything past them, and the discipline she practises is real and is hers. The difficulty is that a technique in this setting is reproduced exactly, from a note of how it felt at its best and how to bring that state back on demand. That is the only transmission method anybody here has found, and it has three requirements she cannot meet. She cannot write a note. She cannot be carried to where a note would be taken, because she is the most immobile body on the tier. And there is no second body of her shape in the setting to demonstrate to, because her species' fertility is a template count rather than a body count and this template has been cast once.

So her practice is not undocumented; it is uncommunicable, by the only mechanism available, and she has known that for a very long time. Three guild masters have offered to put a junior to her. She has refused all three and given the same reason each time, which is that a junior would be handed a description of what she does, that the description would be accurate in every part except the one that mattered, and that the part that mattered is what the state feels like from the inside, and there has never been a second inside. She would rather be the last practitioner of a thing than be its first copy.

The crack is thirty-one years old and healed in the only way a mineral frame heals, which is by ceasing to spread. It is the lower plate, and the plate carries most of her weight, and the guild washes the line in lime every year because the washing is the whole of the maintenance a body like hers can receive and because nobody wants to be the year it is not done. She has decided she does not know whether it is the same crack and has said so once.

What she wants is a second body, which is impossible, and a written method, which she cannot write, and one person to tell her whether the state she reaches feels the same from the inside twice. She has asked for that last thing exactly once, of a guild master who did not understand the question and answered it about the weather. She has not asked again.
history: Was cast thirty-one years ago from template two, on a ledge at the far end of the jade cleft, and does not know to within a season when in her own life that happened.
Was keyed into the sill of the working face in the same year and has not been moved since, on the ground that an unkeyed cairnborn settles and cracks.
Opened her first gate at about twenty and has opened all of the gate set since, and has never once been asked what the next one would feel like, because the next one is not there to feel.
Refused a junior in the ninth year, the seventeenth, and the twenty-fourth, on the same grounds each time, and has been described since as refusing to teach out of obstinacy.
Was told once, by a guild master, that her method would need a written form before it could be passed on, and has not repeated the conversation.

personality.summary: Perfectly still and entirely present, which is not the same as patient. She has been the most reliable body in a working cleft for three decades and has spent most of it turning down the one thing that would have made it matter afterwards. She is not serene; she is a person who has made a decision about her own extinction early and has not unmade it since, and the stillness is what that costs rather than what it buys.

reference_stats.summary: She is the most reliable structural reader in the setting and a practitioner of a path that runs out four gates in, and she is the only body of her shape in the world. The part that hurts is not the ceiling. It is that everything she knows can only be transmitted the way this setting transmits anything — from a note of how it felt at its best — and she cannot write one, cannot be moved to where one would be taken, and has nobody to demonstrate to.
strengths: reads load and vibration through her anchor plates at a distance no one else on the cleft can feel, and has never once called a face that did not go

answering a load question has never once been wrong, which is the only kind of record the cleft keeps

her practice cannot be written down, so it is not merely undocumented but uncommunicable by the only method the setting has

reference_stats.combat_read: She cannot fight and does not need to; a cairnborn is not a combatant, she is terrain that has opinions. What she does defensively is decide, thirty-one years ahead of everybody else, when the ceiling above her stops being worth standing under, and she has not once been asked to say so out loud in time for it to be useful.
reference_stats.notes: The advantage and its cost are one body and both come out of the species record as written: load and vibration through anchor plates, one cavity with a slow tidal circulation and no organ pair, the gate set cleared and the yin organs never reached, cast rather than born with a template count for fertility, and a cracked plate that is permanent and spreads. The one link I have authored rather than quoted is the transmission argument — that a technique is reproduced here from a note of how it felt at its best, and that she can meet none of the three requirements for writing such a note. Nothing here invents a technique, a stat or a rule: no method supplies the paired organs, no item moves her off a sill, and the fourth gate is an absence rather than a threshold she has failed. Three-second version: she is the best instrument in the cleft and the last copy of what she knows.
